source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use bright electronic screens immediately before bed to strengthen the normal sleep response","B":"Keep a consistent sleep schedule, reduce evening screen exposure, and avoid late caffeine","C":"Vary bedtime by several hours each night so the body does not become dependent on a schedule","D":"Use caffeine in the evening because stimulant effects generally shorten sleep-onset latency"}}
source_row.rationale: CDC sleep guidance recommends consistent sleep and wake times, turning off electronic devices before bed, and avoiding caffeine later in the day as practical habits that support better sleep.
source_row.source_detail: Better sleep habits section: consistent schedule, electronic devices off before bedtime, avoid afternoon/evening caffeine; May 15, 2024; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.stem: Which teaching point is appropriate for an adult who wants to improve sleep habits?
